bug_semantics: An unauthenticated request supplies a Base64-encoded URL that is decoded and interpolated into a double-quoted ffmpeg command. URL syntax validation does not neutralize shell substitution metacharacters, and execAsync wraps the command in nohup before passing it to shell_exec, enabling arbitrary OS command execution.
flaw_origin: Commit 036052b948a616ec91fe54b5d3ff84e2dd048a4d first added objects/getImageFromVIdeo.php with a decoded GET parameter interpolated unescaped into an ffmpeg command and executed by shell_exec. Its parent c4a64b1a5d2cabbfb3e930423c0be77a5e4c678e has neither that file nor objects/getImage.php. Commit 1d209ed97981582007ebf5cce1280b75fd9298dd only renamed the input parameter from url to base64Url, and a702adc250ce9a08c9265efd9e97be9714ea2d85 only renamed the file, so neither is the atomic first-write BIC.
ai_marker: No AI marker on the BIC: the single-parent 2017 commit has author and committer daniel <daniel@daniel-DC1A-S>, subject 'Get image from streaming', no body or trailers, and no generated-code attribution.
evidence: The BIC diff creates the endpoint with base64_decode($_GET['url']), builds ffmpeg -i {$url}, and calls shell_exec($exec); the parent tree lacks the endpoint. By the vulnerable parent e0c27689f33f253e49799ff5f8f62edd31cdee2e, objects/getImage.php decodes base64Url, objects/security.php performs only FILTER_VALIDATE_URL, and execAsync constructs nohup plus the command and calls shell_exec. Direct fix 78178d11541d44b238c4dfd9241cacb031db3765 adds URL validation, rejects shell metacharacters, applies escapeshellarg, and replaces every affected ffmpeg interpolation with the escaped argument. Tags 3.0 and 3.7 contain the BIC but not the fix; tag 7.0 contains the fix. The authoritative CVE record is PUBLISHED and states versions before 7.0 are affected and 7.0 is patched.
reasoning: The source-to-sink chain and immediate-parent absence establish 036052b948a616ec91fe54b5d3ff84e2dd048a4d as the smallest public first-write of the command-injection flaw. Later parameter and file renames preserve the same vulnerable operation. The direct remediation and release topology close the fix boundary. AI attribution is judged only on the BIC; its 2017 human-authored metadata and complete lack of AI markers support NOT_AI.
